newsitem.title: USA: General Dynamics seeks new trial in pay case.
newsitem.headline: General Dynamics seeks new trial in pay case.

text.p: General Dynamics Corp on Friday said it would ask a judge to set aside a jury verdict awarding $100 million in damages to 98 former managers.
The company said it would seek a new trial in the case, which involves ex-employees who claimed they were pressured into not joining a 1995 class-action lawsuit over back pay.

A Superior Court jury on Thursday awarded $1.8 million to compensate for back overtime and the rest in punitive damages. In a six-week trial, plaintiffs' attorneys argued the company forced them to give up their legal rights while it was planning behind their backs to close its Convair division.

According to Brian Monaghan, one of the attorneys, the workers had been owed more than 20 months of overtime and opted in 1993 to join an action by 1,100 other workers to collect on it. When they returned to work, however, they were told they would lose their jobs if they persisted in the action, according to testimony at the trial.

A year later, the defense contractor announced it was closing the Convair division. At that point, the workers sought to rejoin the class action, but it was too late. So, they filed their own suit in April 1995.
The other action was settled in 1995 when General Dynamics paid out $5.3 million on overtime claims.

Company officials have denied all along that they applied any pressure. In addition, the workers received full salaries and incurred no losses, General Dynamics spokeswoman Norine Lyons said on Friday.

"There were no economic losses, no economic impact at all," she said from the company's headquarters in Falls Church, Virginia. "Do we think it's unfair. You bet. We think it's outrageous," she said, referring to the verdict before Judge Vincent Di Figlia.
"Our conduct was not malicious. This was an administrative error corrected years ago. There was no pressure not to join -- none whatsoever."
